cleanIntro: The Shadow 2 is CZ's competition CZ 75 — steel frame, manual safety, no firing pin block on the base gun, and a trigger deliberately set up so light that the safety can be pushed on with the hammer at half-cock, which CZ warns against. The strip is the CZ 75 pattern: half-cock, align the two scribed lines, tap the slide stop out from the right. Everything below is read off the English section of CZ's CZ SHADOW manual, PDF pages 2 to 22.

steps.title: Find your gun in the versions table before anything else
steps.action: Match your pistol to CZ's versions table. The base CZ Shadow 2 is listed SA/DA, manual safety YES, decocking NO, firing pin safety NO. The Carry is the odd one out — SA/DA with a decocker and an integrated automatic firing pin block instead of a manual safety.
steps.prose: The book covers CZ Shadow 2, Shadow 2 Orange, Shadow 2 OR, Shadow 2 SA, Shadow 2 Target, Shadow 2 Compact, Shadow 2 Carry and CZ 75 SP-01 Shadow in one set of instructions, and the safety fit is not the same down the column. A plain Shadow 2 has NO firing pin safety, which is a real handling fact and not an omission: only the Carry carries the automatic block. The Orange has a removable bushing at the muzzle that changes the strip, and the Target has an adjustable trigger that nothing else in the family has.
steps.quote: Designed particularly for sports shooting up to 50 meters, the CZ Shadow pistol is a semi automatic handgun equipped with locked breech system.
steps.cite: CZ SHADOW — INSTRUCTION MANUAL / MANUAL DE INSTRUCCIONES / NÁVOD NA POUŽITÍ / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MODE D'EMPLOI — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Description and Terminology, p.4

steps.title: The safety section is written to exclude the Carry
steps.action: If your Shadow 2 has a manual safety, this is your section: with the hammer cocked, push the safety up until the red warning dot is covered, which blocks the trigger mechanism and the slide. If your pistol is a Shadow 2 Carry with a decocking lever, this section does not apply to it.
steps.prose: CZ prints the exclusion as the first line under the heading, and on a Shadow the reason is sharper than on a standard CZ 75. Because the Shadow's trigger mechanism has been specially adjusted, the safety CAN be pushed to SAFE with the hammer resting on the safety notch — a position the book explicitly tells you not to use, because cocking the hammer by force or pulling the trigger from there can damage the trigger mechanism. So the safety goes on with the hammer fully cocked and at no other time, and if the trigger mechanism does get damaged CZ says a certified gunsmith repairs it.
steps.quote: The version equipped with a decocking device is not covered in this section!
steps.cite: CZ SHADOW — INSTRUCTION MANUAL / MANUAL DE INSTRUCCIONES / NÁVOD NA POUŽITÍ / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MODE D'EMPLOI — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Operating Instructions — Engaging the Safety, opening line, p.8
steps.warn: On a Shadow 2 with a manual safety there is no firing pin safety. The versions table lists firing pin safety as NO for every variant except the Shadow 2 Carry.

steps.title: And the decocking section excludes every manual-safety Shadow
steps.action: If your pistol is the Shadow 2 Carry, decock it by thumbing the decocking control lever down; the hammer lowers to the safety notch with no need to touch the trigger. If your Shadow 2 has a manual safety, that section does not apply to it.
steps.prose: The mirror-image exclusion is printed at the head of the decocking section. It is a genuine mechanism difference, not wording: the Carry's lever drops the hammer mechanically and its automatic firing pin block keeps the pin still while that happens, and neither of those things exists on a plain Shadow 2. Applying a decocking instruction to a manual-safety Shadow means lowering a cocked hammer by thumb over whatever is in the chamber, which is exactly the operation this exclusion is keeping you out of.
steps.quote: The version equipped with a manual safety is not covered in this section!
steps.cite: CZ SHADOW — INSTRUCTION MANUAL / MANUAL DE INSTRUCCIONES / NÁVOD NA POUŽITÍ / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MODE D'EMPLOI — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Operating Instructions — Decocking, opening line, p.9

steps.title: Magazine out, then look into the chamber
steps.action: Point the pistol in a safe direction. Depress the magazine catch with the thumb or middle finger and let the magazine come out of the frame. Draw the slide back, confirm by eye that the last cartridge has been extracted and ejected, release the slide vigorously forward, then pull the trigger as an aimed safety shot into a safe area.
steps.prose: The Shadow's magazine catch has a finger piece that can be set in three positions, so where it sits under your thumb is a setting rather than a fixed fact — know where yours is before you reach for it. CZ makes the empty magazine well a precondition of disassembly, and on a steel-framed Shadow there is no substitute for looking into the chamber: the pistol has no loaded chamber indicator in the versions table. Do the dry press deliberately and into something that will stop a round.
steps.quote: Draw back the slide and verify the last cartridge has been extracted from the chamber and ejected
steps.cite: CZ SHADOW — INSTRUCTION MANUAL / MANUAL DE INSTRUCCIONES / NÁVOD NA POUŽITÍ / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MODE D'EMPLOI — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Operating Instructions — Unloading the Pistol, p.8
steps.warn: 1. Remove the magazine. The pistol must not be disassembled with the magazine inserted!

steps.title: The trigger adjustments are the Target's, not yours
steps.action: Do not go looking for trigger reach, trigger pull or overtravel screws on a plain Shadow 2. CZ heads that whole section with a statement that it applies to one variant only, and the trigger-pull screw it describes sits in the ejector where a cleaning brush will find it.
steps.prose: This matters during cleaning rather than during shooting: with the slide off, the Target's trigger-pull screw is exposed in the ejector, and a brush worked hard across that area on any Shadow can move a setting that is held only by Loctite. On a Target, CZ sets trigger pull to 10 N at the factory and recommends never going below it, warns that a too-short slack costs reliability, and hands the overtravel and slack screws to a professional workshop. On every other Shadow those screws are simply not there to adjust, and the magazine catch adjustment differs too — the Shadow 2 Compact does not come with an adjustable finger piece at all.
steps.aside: Sight adjustment differs on the same variant: on the Shadow 2 Target windage is a screw on the right side of the rear sight and elevation a screw on top of it, where the rest of the family drifts the rear sight in its dovetail. Both are secured with Loctite 243.
steps.quote: Setting the Trigger Mechanism IT ONLY APPLIES TO THE CZ SHADOW 2 TARGET VARIANT
steps.cite: CZ SHADOW — INSTRUCTION MANUAL / MANUAL DE INSTRUCCIONES / NÁVOD NA POUŽITÍ / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MODE D'EMPLOI — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Operating Instructions — Setting the Trigger Mechanism, heading, p.10

steps.title: Safety OFF, then hammer down to half-cock
steps.action: Put the safety to the "OFF" position so the slide will move. Retract the hammer slightly and release it until it stops on the half-cock (safety) notch.
steps.prose: On a manual-safety Shadow the safety blocks the slide as well as the trigger, so a slide that will not retract is a safety still up rather than a fault. Half-cock then parks the hammer clear of the firing pin and out of the slide's path, which is what makes the alignment step manageable — with the hammer fully down the slide fights it, and with the hammer cocked the mainspring works against your grip. You will feel a small definite catch as the hammer seats.
steps.quote: 2. Put the safety to the "OFF" position, in order to release the movement of the slide.
steps.cite: CZ SHADOW — INSTRUCTION MANUAL / MANUAL DE INSTRUCCIONES / NÁVOD NA POUŽITÍ / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MODE D'EMPLOI — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Maintenance Instructions — Stripping for Cleaning, step 2, p.11
steps.warn: MAKE SURE THAT THERE IS NO CARTRIDGE IN THE CHAMBER — CZ prints this as the third numbered step of the strip, in capitals.

steps.title: Line up the two vertical scribes
steps.action: Put your left thumb through the trigger guard and grip the forward part of the slide firmly with the other hand. Push the slide slightly back until the two vertical lines — one on the rear of the frame, one on the slide — are exactly in line with each other.
steps.prose: Those two short scribes are the take-down index for the whole CZ 75 pattern and the Shadow keeps them. At any other slide position the slide stop's shaft is trapped in the barrel's lower lug and no amount of hitting will move it. The Shadow 2's slide is steel and heavier than a polymer-framed pistol's, so set the alignment deliberately and hold it while the other hand works. Square on, not nearly.
steps.quote: 5. Put your left thumb through the trigger guard and with the other hand grasp the forward part of the slide firmly (Fig. 13). Push the slide slightly back until the two vertical lines on the rear part of the frame and slide are in line with each other.
steps.cite: CZ SHADOW — INSTRUCTION MANUAL / MANUAL DE INSTRUCCIONES / NÁVOD NA POUŽITÍ / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MODE D'EMPLOI — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Maintenance Instructions — Stripping for Cleaning, step 5, p.11

steps.title: Slide stop tapped from the right, drawn out from the left
steps.action: Keeping the lines aligned, tap the slide stop's protruding shaft from the RIGHT side of the pistol — the magazine base serves as the drift — then withdraw the slide stop from the LEFT.
steps.prose: One direction only, and only with the lines in register. If it will not start, the slide has drifted off the index; reset it rather than hitting harder, because the shaft bears directly on the barrel lug and a heavy blow peens the lug on a competition gun that is meant to shoot to a point. Keep a firm hold on the slide throughout — as soon as the stop clears, the recoil spring will drive the slide forward. Using the magazine base rather than a steel punch keeps the stop's head unmarked.
steps.quote: 6. KEEPING THE LINES ALIGNED push (tap) the slide stop from the right hand side of the weapon, e.g. using the magazine base (Fig. 14). Remove the slide stop from the left.
steps.cite: CZ SHADOW — INSTRUCTION MANUAL / MANUAL DE INSTRUCCIONES / NÁVOD NA POUŽITÍ / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MODE D'EMPLOI — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Maintenance Instructions — Stripping for Cleaning, step 6, p.11

steps.title: Slide and barrel forward off the frame
steps.action: Draw the slide with the barrel still inside forward off the front of the frame, supporting both as they leave the rails.
steps.prose: The Shadow runs its slide INSIDE the frame rails like every CZ 75, so the slide leaves a channel rather than lifting off ledges — keep it square and let it travel straight forward. It is under recoil spring tension the whole way, so do not release your grip halfway. On a steel-framed Shadow the rail channels are long and closely fitted, which is where the accuracy comes from and also why levering the slide out at an angle is worth avoiding.
steps.quote: 7. Pull the slide and the barrel forward off the frame.
steps.cite: CZ SHADOW — INSTRUCTION MANUAL / MANUAL DE INSTRUCCIONES / NÁVOD NA POUŽITÍ / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MODE D'EMPLOI — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Maintenance Instructions — Stripping for Cleaning, step 7, p.11

steps.title: Recoil spring and guide out — and the Orange bushing if you have one
steps.action: Invert the slide, lift out the recoil spring and its guide easing the tension off as it comes, then remove the barrel from the slide. If this is a CZ Shadow 2 Orange with a removable bushing, first take out the recoil spring plug, rotate the bushing clockwise 40º with the supplied disassembly tool and slide it out of the slide.
steps.prose: The bushing step is the one real fork in the Shadow strip and it belongs only to the Orange — the plain Shadow 2, the OR, the SA, the Target, the Compact and the Carry have no removable bushing to turn, and looking for one will have you levering at a muzzle that was never made to come apart. On any Shadow the recoil spring rides a separate guide and is not captive, so hold both ends and let the tension off gradually. There is a rubber buffer on the guide; note whether it is still there and what condition it is in as the assembly comes out.
steps.caution: CZ's own warning on reassembly of the Orange: make sure the recoil spring guide does not protrude from the slide. Incorrect assembly may damage the frame and shorten the service life of the recoil spring.
steps.quote: For CZ Shadow 2 Orange with removable bushing, remove the recoil spring plug and rotate the bushing clockwise by 40º and slide it out of the slide (use the disassembly tool provided with the firearm to turn the bushing).
steps.cite: CZ SHADOW — INSTRUCTION MANUAL / MANUAL DE INSTRUCCIONES / NÁVOD NA POUŽITÍ / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MODE D'EMPLOI — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Maintenance Instructions — Stripping for Cleaning, step 8, p.11

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Frame, slide, barrel, recoil spring and guide, plus the slide stop, with the magazine set aside. That is the field strip CZ publishes for the Shadow 2 — the hammer, sear, ejector, extractor and the trigger mechanism all stay in the pistol.
steps.prose: Those pieces reach everything the cleaning section asks for: the bore and chamber from the breech, the breech face and extractor, the slide's interior and the frame's internal rail channels, and the whole outside of the barrel. CZ's closing line after step 9 is that nothing more is needed for routine maintenance, and names the magazine as the one extra item after a heavy session. Unlike most of the CZ range, this book does go further and publishes a firing pin removal and a buffer replacement, both of which are on the deep path.
steps.quote: No further disassembly is needed for routine maintenance. When a great number of cartridges has been fired, it is advisable to also disassemble magazine.
steps.cite: CZ SHADOW — INSTRUCTION MANUAL / MANUAL DE INSTRUCCIONES / NÁVOD NA POUŽITÍ / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MODE D'EMPLOI — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Maintenance Instructions — Stripping for Cleaning, closing note, p.11

deepSteps.title: Check the rubber buffer on the recoil spring guide
deepSteps.action: Look at the rubber buffer fitted on the recoil spring guide. Judge it visually — if it is worn, replace it. CZ recommends a preventative replacement every 1,000 to 1,500 rounds.
deepSteps.prose: The buffer is what takes the slide's impact against the frame, and on a Shadow 2 that impact is a steel slide against a steel frame at competition round counts. It is a visual check, not a measurement: cracking, flattening or a chewed edge is the signal. Doing it on the interval rather than on failure is the point — a buffer that has broken up puts its pieces into the frame and the impact straight into the metal.
deepSteps.quote: A rubber buffer is installed on the recoil spring guide. This buffer serves for buffering the impact of the slide against the firearm frame.
deepSteps.cite: CZ SHADOW — INSTRUCTION MANUAL / MANUAL DE INSTRUCCIONES / NÁVOD NA POUŽITÍ / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MODE D'EMPLOI — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Maintenance Instructions — Buffer Replacement, p.12

deepSteps.title: Firing pin out of the slide — thumb over the stop
deepSteps.action: Push the rear end of the firing pin in with a suitable tool until it is below the level of the firing pin stop, then press the firing pin stop down about 2 mm. Cover the stop with your thumb and pull it completely out of the slide with the other hand.
deepSteps.prose: This is one of the very few places where a CZ book hands the firing pin to the owner rather than to a gunsmith, and it comes with a matching warning: the pin is spring-loaded and the stop is the only thing containing it. Your thumb over the stop is what keeps the pin and its spring in the slide when the stop clears. Do it over a bench with the slide's rear pointed away from your face, and account for the pin, its spring and the stop before you move on.
deepSteps.quote: Be very careful at this stage of the disassembly procedure, as the firing pin is spring-loaded and could fly out, getting lost, or even causing injury.
deepSteps.cite: CZ SHADOW — INSTRUCTION MANUAL / MANUAL DE INSTRUCCIONES / NÁVOD NA POUŽITÍ / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MODE D'EMPLOI — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Maintenance Instructions — Firing Pin Disassembly, p.12
deepSteps.warn: A plain Shadow 2 has no firing pin safety, so the firing pin channel is the only thing standing between a dropped pistol and an inertia strike. Clean it dry and leave it dry; oil in that channel is what turns cold weather into a light primer hit.

deepSteps.title: Magazine base off — read which lock design you have
deepSteps.action: If the magazine base has a hole, push the base catch through it and shift the base slightly forward. If the rear of the magazine has a sliding bottom lock instead, move the lock to its disassembly position and then shift the base forward. Cover the base with your thumb before it leaves the rails.
deepSteps.prose: CZ builds both patterns and the handling differs — a punch used on a sliding-lock magazine only marks it. Once the lock is clear, the base is riding on its guide rails with a long compressed spring under it, and your thumb is the only thing holding that spring. Let it up slowly, over a bench, with the magazine mouth pointed away from your face, and note which way up the follower sits as it comes out; it is handed.
deepSteps.quote: Cover the base with your thumb to prevent losing the magazine spring and with the other hand take off the base from its guiding rails. Be careful during the disassembly as the spring could fly out, or even cause an injury.
deepSteps.cite: CZ SHADOW — INSTRUCTION MANUAL / MANUAL DE INSTRUCCIONES / NÁVOD NA POUŽITÍ / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MODE D'EMPLOI — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Maintenance Instructions — Magazine Disassembly, p.12

deepSteps.title: Reassemble, then stop
deepSteps.action: Wipe the magazine body inside, the follower and the spring dry — no oil in the body — and put the magazine back together. Clean the firing pin and its channel dry, refit the pin and its stop, and go no further into the pistol.
deepSteps.prose: Oil inside a magazine holds grit against the case walls and slows the follower, which on a competition gun shows up as a sluggish last round in a long stage rather than an obvious jam. While the magazine is apart, sight along the feed lips against a known-good one; a spread lip is a magazine to retire, not to bend back. Beyond the magazine, the firing pin and the buffer, CZ says the pistol goes to a competent gunsmith.
deepSteps.quote: No further disassembly of your pistol is recommended. Should your pistol require adjustment or repair be sure the task is entrusted to a competent gunsmith!
deepSteps.cite: CZ SHADOW — INSTRUCTION MANUAL / MANUAL DE INSTRUCCIONES / NÁVOD NA POUŽITÍ / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MODE D'EMPLOI — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Maintenance Instructions — CAUTION following Magazine Disassembly, p.12

cleaning.name: BARREL & CHAMBER
tasks: Clean patch on the rod through barrel and chamber, changing patches, until the last one comes out clean — enough on its own if the Shadow has fired only a few rounds
For a heavily fouled barrel, brush gun cleaning solution in, let it act about 10 minutes, then scrub the barrel out thoroughly
Rod and brush enter from the CHAMBER end and the brush is driven right out of the muzzle before reversing; reversing inside the barrel jams the brush
Dry barrel and chamber with a clean patch and confirm all powder residue and fouling is gone
On a Shadow 2 Orange, also preserve the front part of the barrel and the inner diameter of the bushing

cleaning.name: SLIDE, FRAME RAILS & EJECTOR AREA
tasks: Dry cloth, old toothbrush, brass bristle brush or wooden scraper on the breech face, the extractor and its cut, and the inside of the slide
Clean the frame's INTERNAL rail channels — the Shadow's slide runs inside them and that is where a steel-framed CZ collects grit
Work carefully around the ejector: on a Shadow 2 Target the trigger-pull adjustment screw lives in it and is held only by Loctite
Preserving oil or paraffin oil may be used here — never the barrel cleaning agent, which stays in the joints and causes corrosion later
Check that no cloth particles or brush bristles are lodged in any part of the pistol

cleaning.name: PRESERVING
tasks: With barrel, chamber and all accessible parts clean and dry, wipe them with a cloth soaked in gun oil or apply it as a spray, then remove all excess
Keep solvent off the fibre optic front sight insert — wipe the sight body dry rather than scrubbing it
At very low temperatures remove the oil from all accessible parts or use a lubricant made for those conditions
Thick preserving grease is for long-term storage in severe climates only and comes off every part before use
Pull a dry patch through the barrel before shooting

reassembly: Barrel into the inverted slide first, then the recoil spring and guide with its buffer in place.

On a Shadow 2 Orange: bushing back into the slide and rotated home, then the recoil spring plug — and confirm the recoil spring guide does NOT protrude from the slide, which CZ warns can damage the frame and shorten the spring's life.
Run the slide onto the frame rails from the front and push it back until the two vertical lines are again in register; the slide stop will not enter at any other position.
Insert the slide stop from the LEFT and press it home flush; thumb pressure is enough once the lines are square.
Let the slide run forward, cycle it by hand once, and check the slide stop has stayed seated.
If the magazine catch finger piece was moved, secure its screw with medium strength Loctite 243 before the pistol is used.
fncheck: Magazine out and chamber confirmed empty. With the hammer cocked, a manual-safety Shadow 2's safety should go up and block both trigger and slide; do NOT test it with the hammer at half-cock, because CZ states the specially adjusted trigger mechanism allows the safety on from there and can be damaged by cocking or pulling against it. The hammer should catch cleanly at half-cock and sit clear of the firing pin. Cycle the slide by hand: the slide stop should stay flush, an empty magazine should lock the slide back, and the trigger should reset with a clean single-action break. On a Shadow 2 Carry, check instead that the decocker drops the hammer without the trigger moving and springs back up on its own.
